title: Understand the moon phases and the arrival of the full moon
seoTitle: Moon phases and the full moon: understand the cycle
subtitle: Twenty-nine and a half day lunar cycle brings the full moon on August twenty-eighth
excerpt: Learn how the moon phases and the lunar cycle work, and what to expect from the arrival of the full moon, a period of great visibility and intensity.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Olhar Digital, Correio Braziliense, O POVO
contentHtml:
The lunar cycle and the movement of the moon phases arouse great interest, especially with the approach of the full moon scheduled for August twenty-eighth. The lunation has an average duration of twenty-nine and a half days, a period during which the satellite goes through the four main phases.

How the lunar cycle works

A lunation is the time interval between new moons, with an average duration of twenty-nine and a half days. During this period, the celestial body goes through the main phases of new, waxing, full, and waning, as well as the intermediate phases.

The phases occur according to the position of the moon in relation to the sun and the earth. As it orbits the planet, different portions of its face appear illuminated to observers on the ground.

The energy of the new and waxing moon

During the new moon, the satellite positions itself between the earth and the sun, leaving the illuminated side facing the sun and the dark side facing the earth. This phase marks the beginning of a new lunar cycle and is associated with planning.

After the new moon, the waxing phase appears, where an illuminated strip grows night after night. This stage symbolizes growth, development, and the execution of previously planned projects.

The peak with the full moon

During the full moon, the earth is positioned between the sun and the moon, allowing the lunar side facing us to receive full light. It is the period of greatest luminous intensity and magnetism.

The phase is characterized by intensified emotions and maximum visibility, a moment when the moon rises on the horizon at the exact instant the sun sets.

The conclusion in the waning moon

After the full moon, the light begins to gradually decrease until it reaches the waning quarter and restarts the cycle. The waning phase symbolizes reflection, the completion of tasks, and preparation for new beginnings.
